subject.title: `before_agent_run` receives no input provenance; several producers never stamp it — internal wakes look like user input at the gate

question: Should `before_agent_run` become an origin-aware policy boundary using the existing `InputProvenance` taxonomy, and what authoritative kind should each internal producer family stamp?
rationale: The code change is bounded, but the provenance classifications become a public plugin security contract and determine which unattended runs plugins may trust or block.

options.title: Add additive provenance contract
options.body: Expose optional `InputProvenance`, define every producer classification centrally, preserve undefined for genuinely unknown origins, and document fail-open plugin guidance.

options.title: Defer pending broader provenance design
options.body: Keep the issue open until maintainers define a comprehensive provenance contract spanning hooks, session events, transcripts, and future producer types.

options.title: Keep the gate content-only
options.body: Decline origin-aware enforcement and clarify that `before_agent_run` cannot distinguish human, inter-session, and internal triggers.

recommendation.title: Add additive provenance contract
recommendation.body: Expose optional `InputProvenance`, define every producer classification centrally, preserve undefined for genuinely unknown origins, and document fail-open plugin guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal is recent work on the embedded hook execution path where the contract must be propagated consistently.
